summary.text: Amanda Green is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 2nd Congressional District seat. A Florida State University graduate, she describes a career in operations and pricing roles supporting global health programs, beginning with a USAID partner organization. She is running on an affordability, anti-corruption and government-accountability platform.

paragraphs.text: Earned a bachelor's degree (2015) and a graduate degree (2017) from Florida State University, according to Ballotpedia; she says she studied international development, economics and public administration.
Began her career with what she calls a leading USAID partner organization.
Says she worked for about a decade as an operations director and pricing expert supporting global health programs, famine monitoring systems, and relief efforts in Ukraine.
According to WFSU, her campaign website says she worked for a subsidiary of USAID until the agency was cut back after President Trump returned to office.
Entered the race after Rep. Neal Dunn announced his retirement; Ballotpedia lists no earlier campaigns or offices for her.
Won the August 18, 2026 four-way Democratic primary over Yen Bailey, Nicholas Zateslo and Brice Barnes; WFSU reports endorsements from the AFL-CIO and Leon County Sheriff Walt McNeil.
Campaign priorities she lists include lowering housing and gas costs, banning congressional stock trading, enacting term limits, and holding regular in-person town halls across the district.
